points.why: It shows each side's local fix landing on the other and notes that nobody owns the shared outcome, but it never frames them as natural allies with a common goal, so it never names the Accidental Adversaries structure.
It traces volume, weak candidates, more screening and rejection, slower fills and back to more volume, and explicitly calls it a reinforcing loop.
It says both sides are reacting sensibly and each reads the other's reaction as the cause when it is really the effect.
It recommends shared time-to-fill and quality metrics, calibrated intake on the candidate profile, and presenting the loop as a joint system problem with shared ownership.

pitfalls.why: It opens with 'Neither is right' and keeps a balanced, system-level framing throughout.
It uses 'volume escalation' only casually and never casts the two groups as rivals in an Escalation archetype.
